newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Twenty charged in Bangladesh's Mujib killing trial.
newsitem.headline: Twenty charged in Bangladesh's Mujib killing trial.

text.p: A total of 20 people have been formally charged for their alleged involvement in the killing of Bangladesh's independence leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman in a 1975 army coup, police said on Tuesday.
They said a court dealing with the trial on Monday completed the laying of charges and set April 21 for the hearing to formally begin.
The accused, mostly retired army officers, have been charged with murder, conspiracy and concealing evidence, police said.
Police said only six of the 20 accused were in custody while others had absconded, some of them believed to have fled the country.
Five of the six, including four ex-army officers and ex-politician Taheruddin Thakur who served as Mujib's information minister, appeared in court on Monday and pleaded not guilty.
Zobaida Rashid, wife of co-accused retired colonel Shahriar Rashid, failed to appear because she was ill, her attorney told the court.
Mujib, father of Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, was killed in an army coup in August 1975. He led Bangladesh, formerly East Pakistan, to independence from Pakistan in 1971.
The trial over his killing had to wait until Hasina took office last June because his successors had passed a law shielding the masterminds of the 1975 coup from the law.
Bangladesh's parliament repealed the law in November.
